To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of LiDAR, Landsat, and machine learning methods can generate accurate and precise estimates of forest vegetation properties (canopy cover and vegetation height) that are important to forest management, forest monitoring, and land cover and land cover change classification.

(1) machine learning techniques are able to model vegetation height and canopy coverage from satellite data and LiDAR data with high accuracy and precision; (2) the use of ensemble methods improves significantly the prediction accuracy; and (3) the use of LiDAR satellite and data integration can generate cost effective realistic maps of the vegetation height, and consequently generate forest canopy cover maps to be used in the forest management and monitoring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods that can be applied to the estimation and mapping of forest vegetation height and canopy coverage.

the integration of remote sensing data and the application of advanced machine learning techniques in order to generate continuous forest maps that can be used to improve the monitoring and management of forest ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach of using LiDAR and Landsat data, and machine learning techniques, is able to provide realistic and accurate vegetation height and canopy maps of Slovenia.

the use of machine leaning methods for the integration of LiDAR, Landsat data and the generation of forest vegetation maps is promising and can be successfully used for the generation and management of forest vegetation maps in the Slovenian forest ecosystems.
machine learning methods are a powerful and effective tool for modeling and mapping of forest vegetation height and canopy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a methodology for generating continuous maps of forest vegetation height and canopy covers.
we have successfully used the combination of LiDAR, Landsat and machine learning methods to generate realistic and continuous forest maps.

the integration of LiDAR with satellite data can provide cost effective realistic estimates for the vegetation height and the canopy cover, as well as the generation of forest vegetation maps that can be used in forest ecosystem management and monitoring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of satellite data and LiDAR data is a promising way for estimating forest properties.
the use of machine-learning methods can provide more accurate and reliable information about vegetation height and canopy coverage than the use of traditional regression techniques.

the use of machine and ensemble learning algorithms can be a promising approach for generating accurate and cost-effective maps of forest properties, and can be a useful tool in forest management and ecosystem monitoring.
